purpose: Supervised alpha study with genuine ASL signers: measure raw recognition separately from transcript safety (suggestion decisions), and collect consented correction feedback. Development sessions inform design; held-out sessions are sealed until a candidate recognizer is frozen.

participants.eligibility: Adults (18+) who use ASL regularly and consent in their preferred language or with an interpreter. Deaf, hard-of-hearing and hearing signers welcome; at least one Deaf signer per split is a target.

split.rule: A signer's split is fixed at enrolment, before any of their sessions is recorded or inspected, from the pseudonym and this plan's salt: development if the first byte of SHA-256(salt + ':' + pseudonym) is even, held_out otherwise. Every session of a signer stays in that split. Held-out sessions are never summarised while a candidate is being developed.

camera_position.label: Camera in front at about eye level, upper body in view
Laptop on a desk: camera below eye level, looking up
Camera about 30 degrees to one side

lighting.label: Even, bright light on the face and hands
Window or lamp behind the signer

session_conditions.rotation: Session 2 uses the next (camera_position, lighting) pair from the list below, in enrolment order, so all pairs are covered across signers.

confusable_signs.selection: Glosses whose WLASL clips triggered a starter rule in the PR #54/#55 analysis (STARTER-RELIABILITY.md), chosen by gloss only. New recordings are captured; no WLASL clip is reused.

items.instruction: Adjust or push up your glasses (or mime it)
Push your hair aside from your forehead
Wave to someone across the room
Scratch your chin or touch your mouth briefly
Rest a hand on your chest, then move it away
Pick up a cup and drink (or mime it)
Type on a keyboard or use your phone for a few seconds
Keep your hands still and visible for a few seconds

unsupported_signs.policy: The facilitator or an independent fluent reviewer chooses two ASL signs absent from the installed ASL-2000 + starter vocabulary before the session; the participant signs them without being told what SignRelay supports.

sequences.purpose: Signed one after another without pausing, to exercise rapid successive suggestions and transcript ordering.

tasks.order: Blocks in a fixed order (starter signs, everyday movements, confusable signs, unsupported signs, sequences) with tasks shuffled inside each block by a seed derived from the pseudonym and session, so order effects are balanced and reproducible.

measures.raw_recognition: For each trial, the first word SignRelay produced (any source, suggested or automatic) during the trial window, compared with the expected gloss; or none (abstention).
measures.transcript_safety: Words that entered the transcript during the trial window, automatically or because the participant added them, compared with what they signed.
measures.decisions: Added, dismissed, timed out or replaced, for every suggestion.
measures.correction: The participant's own report: correct, wrong word, missed, unexpected word, tracking problem, and optionally the gloss actually signed (from the plan's gloss list).
measures.latency: Time from the participant pressing Start (or the sign onset they report) to the first output.

privacy: No video, image, landmark or audio is stored by the study session tool; it records task ids, SignRelay's outputs, decisions and the participant's selected corrections, with times relative to the session start. Video recording for training is a separate, separately consented activity (/field-test). See CONSENT-AND-PRIVACY.md.
release_claim: A plan, not observed trials. No accuracy figure may be cited from this study until sessions have actually taken place, and held-out figures only from a frozen candidate.
